text.p: Three-times Wimbledon champion Boris Becker denied on Thursday he had left his native Germany for good and said he and his wife Barbara had not yet made any such decision about their future.
"Suspicions that I have turned by back on Germany are false. My wife and I have not yet made any such decision," Becker said in a statement released by his lawyer in Munich.
Becker added he had done nothing wrong from a tax point of view and said the behaviour of tax investigators, who raided his Munich house in December, would not play a role in such a decision.

"We would not make such an important decision dependent on the behaviour of the financial administration, whose proceedings up to now I disapprove of," Becker said. "I have done nothing wrong from a tax point of view and I am sure that will be recognised by the financial authorities."
Becker's statement came after the German media reported on Monday he was leaving Germany for good and moving to a luxury home in the United States.

Becker flew to Miami on Monday and the German media reported he was planning to make a new home on the exclusive Fisher Island just off Miami Beach, where fellow tennis player Jim Courier owns a home.
His wife Barbara and three-year-old son Noah arrived in Florida last weekend.
But Becker said he was there to play at the Lipton Championships in Key Biscayne at the end of the week.

The former world number one had said last year that he wanted to move to the United States when his son was old enough to begin school. But after the raid by German tax investigators on his Munich house in his absence in December an angry Becker warned he could leave his country sooner.

Becker and his wife, who is black, have said they want Noah to attend school in the United States to avoid the pressures in Germany of having a famous father, and so that he might be able to lead a more normal life in a multi-racial society.

Axel Meyer-Woelden, Becker's lawyer, on Thursday denied media reports that the Becker family had held a farewell party and said Noah's room was empty because the family always took all the child's belongings with them when they travelled.
Meyer-Woelden said Becker had sold his old car only in order to buy a new Mercedes.
The mass-circulation daily Bild, which on Monday ran a story headlined: "Boris's bitter farewell", said on Thursday there was still a chance the beloved tennis star could stay in his country.
